description:
This plugin allows users to sign in through an SSO provider (such as Google, Facebook, or your own provider). This enables one-click signin.
Review documentation at https://github.com/MaxRink/jellyfin-plugin-sso
name: SSO-Auth
overview: Authenticate users against an SSO provider.

versions.changelog:
Adds sign-out, post-login destinations, username mappings and SSO-only login.

## Signing out of the provider
`/SSOViews/logout?provider=NAME` ends the Jellyfin session and then the session at the identity provider. It uses the provider's `end_session_endpoint`, or the new per-provider **Logout URL** when the provider does not publish one. **Authelia does not publish one**, so set the Logout URL to `https://auth.example.com/logout` there. Jellyfin 12 has no hook in its own sign-out button, so add the link yourself (see the README).

## Sending users to a page after login
Add `?returnUrl=/movies` (or `?url=`) to the start URL. Only paths on this server are accepted; anything else falls back to the home page. A Quick Connect code still takes priority.

## Username mappings
Per provider, map a provider username to a different Jellyfin username, for example `{"max.mustermann": "Max"}`. Matching an existing account by name already ignored upper and lower case; that now also applies to links created before 6.0.

## SSO-only login
One switch turns off password login for every account that has an SSO link. Accounts without a link are never touched, so a local administrator keeps a password if the provider is unreachable, and an exemption list keeps named accounts on passwords.

## Pushed Authorization with Basic credentials
New option **Send Client Credentials As Basic Auth**. Pushed Authorization Requests always use a Basic header while the token request normally uses the body, and a provider can only be set one way. Turn this on together with `client_secret_basic` at the provider to keep Pushed Authorization enabled.

## Other
- The plugin logo now ships in the package, so the card in the dashboard shows it.
- Fixed a configuration property that handed out a throwaway dictionary, which silently dropped writes to an empty link list.
Show the SSO settings page in the dashboard sidebar (Plugins section), like other configurable plugins. No functional changes otherwise; see 6.0.0.0 for the Jellyfin 12 release notes.

First stable release for **Jellyfin 12** (`net10.0`, plugin ABI `12.0.0.0`, built against `Jellyfin.Controller`/`Jellyfin.Model` 12.0.0). For Jellyfin 10.11 keep using the 4.x/5.x releases.

This release also consolidates fixes and features from the wider `jellyfin-plugin-sso` fork network. All adopted work is GPL-3.0; the original authors are preserved in the commit history and credited in the README **Acknowledgements**.

## Upgrade notes
- **Account linking** now starts from the self-service page (`/SSOViews/linking`) while signed in, via the authenticated `POST {mode}/StartLink/{provider}`. The unauthenticated `?isLinking=true` start is refused. Linking states are single-use, bound to the provider and expire after 10 minutes; SAML responses are validated against the request they answer; an identity already linked to another user is refused.
- **OpenID links are keyed by the `sub` claim** instead of the username. Existing username-keyed links are migrated automatically on the next login.
- The release asset and plugin folder are now named `sso-auth_<version>` (package name aligned with the runtime plugin name so Jellyfin can remove superseded versions on upgrade).
- New per-provider option `disableUsernameAccountAdoption` (OIDC and SAML): refuse a first login whose username matches an unlinked local account instead of adopting it. Off by default.
- `enabledFolders` is now always granted, also when folder roles are enabled.

## Fixes
- Linking page works on Jellyfin 12 (it now authenticates with the `Authorization` header; the legacy header is ignored by Jellyfin 12).
- Requests to the identity provider go through Jellyfin's dual-stack HTTP client with a 30 s timeout and report 502/504 naming the endpoint instead of hanging for 100 s (#2).
- Pre-existing local/LDAP accounts keep their auth provider; `defaultProvider` owns plugin-created accounts from the start; default library access is only stripped when the plugin manages permissions.
- Claim values are no longer logged on denied logins; only enabled providers are advertised; provider-supplied values are escaped on the linking page; warnings when discovery trust checks are disabled.
- Null-safe scopes/roles, persisted redirect path style and unregister provider switch, 404 on unlinking an unknown name, real server version on SSO sessions, disposed avatar downloads, materialised link queries, admin-page checkbox state reset, config-page links open again.
- Removed the vulnerable `System.Security.Cryptography.Xml` package (provided by the .NET 10 shared framework) and the unused F# helper project.

## Features
- `roleClaim` accepts several space-separated claim paths and JSON-object-keyed roles (Zitadel); the device-code flow uses the same parser.
- Inline `data:image/...;base64` avatars (Kanidm, Pocket ID).
- Cloudflare Access UserInfo failures are reported clearly (`doNotLoadProfile`).

## Verification
Built warning-free with the .NET 10 SDK, unit tests pass, and the end-to-end test (authentik + `jellyfin/jellyfin:12.0` + Playwright) covers the OIDC login, the linking page and the StartLink flow.
